_why: Recorded recall and precision per scored form. A ratchet, like the CSS ones: these only ever go DOWN by a deliberate edit that says why in its commit message. A number going up is free and should be re-recorded in the same change that earned it, or the next change gets to lose it silently.
_readMe: src/editor/adapters/pdf/corpus/README.md, section 'The scored corpus'. MOBI-13 has the programme and the one decision still open.

pdkef-practice-form.note: Self-labelling: the nine AcroForm widgets are the truth, exact to the point. The one miss is the signature field, which collectTextFieldWidgets does not read by design (MOBI-11) - so this form reports a real scope line rather than a flattering 100%.

health.note: Recall reproduces the spike's recorded 86.7% exactly. Precision is 80.2% here against a recorded 94.2% because this fixture is geometry-only: with no text layer, formCells' own-text filter never fires and the explanatory cells it would drop stay as false positives. 80.2% is the spike's own pre-fix number, which is the tell. See MOBI-13's fixture decision.
health.derived: geometry-only reduction of the annotated original; see note

itc101.note: 55.4% here against 82.0% on the real source PDF, and the gap is still this fixture. 44 of the 62 checkbox targets are drawn as glyphs, which collectCheckboxGlyphs reads from the text layer the geometry-only reduction removed. The 18 that do match are the children table's narrow tick columns, which formCells recovers from ink alone (MOBI-11), which is why this row is no longer a flat checkbox zero. See MOBI-13's fixture decision.
